According to today's guest, the Home Depot's VP of Asset Protection Scott Glenn, shoplifting is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to retail theft; what is really bedeviling companies like the Home Depot is something called organized retail crime, heists by criminal outfits that seek to nab large quantiles of merchandise that eventually ends up in the black market. Jason Crow (D-CO) says Congress has the constitutional authority to end the war with Iran, arguing the conflict is costing hundreds of billions of dollars and contributing to higher energy prices. Rep. Crow says the US cannot permanently prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon through military action alone and calls for a permanent, verifiable diplomatic agreement. Rep. Crow says Democrats should reinstate ACA subsidies to bring health-care premiums under control and argues that Congress urgently needs a nonpartisan approach to AI regulation and guardrails. Crawford says he likes the idea of President Trump’s proposed dividend checks but that any spending decision should be considered in light of the national debt. title: Scrutiny of Sánchez Grows With Release of Ceuta Papers
title_cn: 随着休达文件的发布，对桑切斯的审查不断加强
summary: Pedro Sánchez had hoped to draw a line under his government’s handling of the migration crisis in Ceuta by declassifying documents late last night. Instead, it’s had the opposite effect.
